articles.summary: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa says he does not 'feel fear' after defeat at Ipswich left his side winless in six games and bottom of the Premier League.
articles.body:
Six games, no wins and bottom of the table - it is fair to say it has been a difficult start to life as a Premier League manager for Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

The Cottagers were on the cusp of victory at Ipswich on Saturday but the hosts scored twice after the 88th minute to snatch a 2-1 win.

It is the second successive game in the league that Fulham have led approaching the final few minutes, only to concede.

It means they have just two points to show so far, increasing the pressure on Arbeloa to improve his side's fortunes.

"I never worry about my position," said former Real Madrid manager Arbeloa.

"I don't feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision and you need to show confidence to your players.

"For me I am so happy with many things that they are doing. I know it is not easy for them.

"It's not about my position, it is about Fulham 's position. That is the most important thing. Obviously it is just six games, but it is true we need points."

When Marco Silva was appointed Fulham boss in 2021 he brought a stability to the club that ensured they were competitive in the Premier League, without ever really being in danger of being relegated.

Silva departed in the summer to become head coach of Benfica and in appointing Arbeloa as his replacement, Fulham were undoubtedly taking a bit of a gamble.

The former Liverpool and Real Madrid player arrived with limited managerial experience at senior level, having had a brief spell in charge of Real Madrid from January until May this year.

The biggest problem Fulham have had under him is conceding late goals, with his side having let in goals in the final 15 minutes in four of their six Premier League matches.

Despite that, Arbeola was defiant after the Ipswich defeat, insisting he is right man for the job at Fulham , and he can handle the pressure of needing to turn things around.

"Maybe you don't know me but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world," he said.

"Maybe you don't know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.

"So, it is normal in football. It is normal for players, it is normal for coaches and everybody that is around a team.

"I think pressure is something that is important for me and I like it."

The Ipswich match marked the first of three games in a row where Fulham face a newly promoted side.

They host Hull on Saturday, 17 October before travelling to Coventry a week later and failure to win at least one of those fixtures would increase the pressure further on Arbeloa.

"We need to take a hard look at ourselves," said Ryan Sessegnon, who had put Fulham ahead at Ipswich.

"It's a bit of mentality thing at the moment. We need to try and demand more from ourselves.

"We need to set higher standards for ourselves because it's going to be a hard season."

articles.title: Barcelona beat Getafe as Gordon scores his first goal
articles.summary: Barcelona make it six wins from six with a 3-0 win against Getafe as Anthony Gordon scores his first goal for club.
articles.body:
Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.

England international Gordon opened the scoring in the second minute, and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season.

French defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal’s cross to cap Barca’s solid win against Jose Bordalas’s side at Camp Nou.

Barca moved five points clear of second-placed Atletico Madrid, who won 2-1 at Alaves earlier, and lead Real Madrid, fourth, by nine points before Los Blancos host Villarreal later on.

Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil.

Flick replaced him with former Arsenal striker and Selecao compatriot Jesus, and his side came roaring out of the blocks.

Gordon, who has impressed since joining before this season, grabbed his first Barca goal with a low deflected effort after bundling his way past three players.

The winger was Barca’s brightest spark in the first half, continuing his fine goalscoring form for England in the recent Nations League matches.

Barca defender Eric Garcia forced a save from Getafe goalkeeper David Soria with a drive from distance as Flick’s side controlled the game.

Getafe defender Zaid Romero gave the ball away in his own box for Barca’s second, passing it straight to Jesus, who stroked into the bottom corner.

Soria denied Olmo before Yamal teed up Kounde for the third.

The defender, making a record 194th appearance for Barca for a French player, overtaking Eric Abidal, was on hand to turn home from close range from teenage star Yamal’s cross.

Barca, who also won their Champions League opener, have nine victories from nine matches across all competitions.

images.caption: Anthony Gordon of Barcelona celebrates scoring his team’s first goal [David Ramos/Getty Images]

articles.title: Chelsea ready to attack key run of games as Noni Madueke shines in new Arsenal role - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers dissect the action from another busy day of Premier League football as Chelsea prepare for a key run of games by thrashing Bournemouth, while Noni Madueke caught the eye in a new position for Arsenal in the champions' come-from-behind win over Leeds
articles.body:
Chelsea's season is set to be shaped by the run of games they have before the November international break. After a mixed start to Xabi Alonso's reign, he is in need of a strong run in the Premier League to boost the bid to return to Champions League football, while a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool could be a launchpad for early silverware.

His Chelsea side showed how they're going to go about it on Saturday, blowing away Bournemouth with their attacking power.

Joao Pedro is fit again and still firing. Cole Palmer was classy and looks recovered from the issue which forced him out of England duty and buoyed by a new Chelsea contract. Morgan Rogers is in form and connecting with both in style. And a certain Jordan Henderson has developed an ability to crack in stunning goals.

Moises Caicedo's first start brought extra punch in midfield. There was, though, some nervousness when Bournemouth bundled one back, such has been Chelsea's poor defensive record this season. But while Alonso was preparing a double change to intervene, Chelsea scored two more. That looks like it will be their way for now, as they aim to blast their way into a position to push for success this season. Peter Smith

Noni Madueke can be a frustrating player to watch at times. Arsenal and Chelsea fans have seen it. England fans witnessed it at the World Cup. Even Mikel Arteta feels it.

"When I haven't liked so much what he was doing or it wasn't impacting the game, I made certain decisions, he has accepted them," the Arsenal manager said. But this was a display where Madueke shone - and led the way - in a slightly different role.

Madueke lined up on the left wing for Arsenal against Leeds. He has only started two games for the Gunners in that position - the first came 14 months ago in the 5-0 win over Leeds. That was his full Arsenal debut.

But with Christos Tzolis injured, Arsenal have been a bit short at left wing. Many expected Eberechi Eze to fill in - but Madueke got the nod and as Arteta said: "He took his chance."

Madueke was Arsenal's best forward player on the day, creating three chances - that Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard should put away.

He then played a big role in the equaliser, with his right-footed cross finding Ben White at the back post, who then set up Riccardo Calafiori.

Madueke was the only Arsenal player to complete a cross against Leeds - and he completed five crosses from six attempts. He was making things happen - he has been doing it for a while in front of Arteta.

"What he's done is raise the level. And in training he's been the best player in the last 10 days. You could see that every time he was in and around the ball he looked a threat."

Like other signings last season, including Viktor Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi, Madueke's Arsenal career was at risk of stalling. Has he now found a second wind in a new position? Sam Blitz

It is a mark of the progress Leeds United have made that Daniel Farke was heartbroken to leave the home of the Premier League champions empty-handed.

Last season, they lost four and five-nil to Arsenal. At the Emirates on Saturday, Leeds were comfortably the better side for nearly an hour, limiting Arsenal to just five shots before James Justin fired Farke's side ahead after 55 minutes.

In the immediate aftermath of their opener, Leeds kept pushing and Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a whisker away from doubling the advantage from Jayden Bogle's cross. If that goes in, we might be talking about a completely different outcome.

Farke set Leeds up to go for it at Arsenal, spurred on by Brighton's blueprint before the international break, and he was nearly rewarded for his ambition. The unbeaten run might be over, but Leeds can keep looking up. They should be considered European contenders. Zinny Boswell

Alvaro Arbeloa is going to have to learn quickly if he is to survive the Premier League.

Ipswich's 2-1 victory over Fulham was a painful reminder that managing at the highest level is about more than having a tactical plan. It is about understanding the physical demands of this league, recognising the momentum shifts and knowing when to make the right substitutions.

Fulham's decision to retreat in the closing stages was almost Thomas Tuchel-esque in England's approach against Argentina. The invitation was there for Ipswich to pile on the pressure, and they duly obliged, scoring twice late on to turn the game around. Just like Argentina did.

Bringing on the lightweight Manuel Ángel for a Premier League debut felt like a gamble at precisely the wrong moment. With Ipswich turning the contest into a physical battle, Fulham needed players capable of matching that intensity, winning second balls and relieving the pressure.

Instead, Ipswich's power and directness came to the fore when it mattered most. Lewis Jones

"At Villa Park, we have played three matches and we did not win until now," said Unai Emery after seeing his side held by Kristoffer Ajer's goal that earned Brentford their 2-2 draw. This place was once a fortress but it is proving trickier for a much-changed squad.

There will be patience with the players, particularly given that Nicolas Jackson, scorer of Aston Villa's opening goal, has made a promising start and there is such excitement about the potential of talented new signings like Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye.

But could the empty North Stand be another factor in their home form too? Villa Park feels unusually open with no supporters there and the Brentford supporters were likening the atmosphere to that of a library right from the early stages of the contest.

"It just feels wrong, doesn't it? I don't know what it is," said Bees boss Keith Andrews. "I have got a little bit of OCD, so maybe it's that, if there's a whole stand missing it doesn't quite sit well with me. Naturally, it's not going to generate the type of atmosphere.

"I have to say, I love coming here. When I was growing up as a kid, some Irish legends played here, Ray Houghton, Paul McGrath, Andy Townsend, so it's always been a special place for me and you can feel the history of it. With a stand missing, it is a bit different."

Emery has been sanguine about the situation publicly, accepting that it is one step back to take two forwards by increasing the capacity. But Villa Park is less claustrophobic for its visitors right now and that is far from ideal for a club so reliant on its home form. Adam Bate

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris will be praying Brian Brobbey's hamstring injury is not too serious after his side drew a blank against the 10 men of Brighton at the Stadium of Light.

The striker, who scored a brilliant hat-trick in the Black Cats' previous outing at Manchester City, picked up the knock while recently on international duty with the Netherlands, meaning a first Premier League start of the season for Wilson Isidor.

The Haiti international nearly gave the hosts an early lead when his sliding opportunity was deflected, while after the break he was involved in Pascal Struijk's dismissal, having been brought down by the Brighton defender while through on goal.

However, Isidor was unable to find the net, meaning Sunderland have now lost back-to-back league games on Wearside without scoring for the first time since April/May 2017 as they slipped to 16th in the table. Rich Morgan

articles.title: Man Utd 1-1 Tottenham: Dominic Solanke rescues dramatic draw for 10-man Spurs at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Spurs came from behind to rescue an unlikely draw at Old Trafford with 10 men; Bryan Mbeumo scored the opener; Dominic Solanke atoned for a series of missed chances to level the game in stoppage time; Man Utd were booed off the pitch
articles.body:
The point at least lifts Spurs off the foot of the table, but Roberto De Zerbi's side remain marooned in the relegation zone, without a league victory since May.

Their predicament can be summed up by three cases of extreme wastefulness and one of ill-discipline, with Dominic Solanke particularly guilty of spurning the chances that might have seen his side take a comfortable first-half lead.

Instead, it was Bryan Mbeumo who broke the deadlock in the 73rd minute, combining with Matheus Cunha in the box and turning smartly to guide a clinical finish across Antonin Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the game in the ascendancy but were hurtling towards their fourth loss of an already chaotic campaign, made worse by a moment of madness from Rodrigo Bentancur, who saw red for a headbutt motion towards Luke Shaw five minutes after the goal. The incident sparked a touchline brawl between both benches.

As emotions ran high, De Zerbi's mission looked hopeless. But Spurs did not give up, and were rewarded with a leveller in stoppage time when Solanke glanced a header past a static Senne Lammens.

Neither manager is likely to be satisfied with the outcome.

Man Utd were booed off the pitch at half time and full time, stuck in the midst of their worst start to a season for 40 years. Spurs' plight, meanwhile, is arguably more damning still. After the points were shared, it's perhaps a result that leaves more questions than answers for both.

3: MISS! Lucas Bergvall pounces on a poor Lammens pass to put Solanke through on goal, but the striker can't punish the mistake.

21: HUGE CHANCE! Savio sets up Kudus, who hooks a first-time shot wide of Lammens' right-hand post.

34: SHOT! Mbeumo feeds Amad on the counter, but his low shot is easily saved by Kinsky.

42: CHANCE! Solanke plays in Conor Gallagher, who just needs to pull the trigger but he takes too long and allows Lammens to save.

49: CHANCE! Spurs pass up another chance as Savio drives into the box and rolls the ball back into the six-yard box but Shaw clears.

51: OVER! Savio gets to the byline and crosses for Solanke, who balloons over from six yards out.

73: GOAL! Mbeumo scores smart opener on the turn, beating Kinsky with a clean, low drive.

90+2: GOAL! Martinez is distracted as Sandro Tonali's cross comes in, losing sight of the ball and allowing Solanke to glance a header home.

Carrick with soul-searching to do after 'worrying' performance

"Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He'd missed some big chances and was captain for the first time.

"They were the better team by far. If they'd left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.

"Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead."

"I do not see enough connections in that midfield and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back.

"Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.

"Their energy levels are not good enough and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.

"The squad is not good or strong enough and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect."

"We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it.

"I'm not happy with the amount of points, I'm not hiding from that. We need to put things in a positive direction quickly.

"We have to be more streetwise and stubborn in the moment. It doesn't change my belief, or confidence in the players. We can be a really good team.

"We don't want to start games like that, it was challenging. They worked through it, got themselves in a good position, and couldn't see the game out. That's the most disappointing thing.

"I don't feel let down bty players making mistakes but we've all got to help each other be better."

De Zerbi pleased with different Spurs character

"We did not deserve to lose, for sure. Today, for the first time we showed we're a team. We played for team-mates, stayed inside of the game in every situation. We attack and defend as a team.

"Suffer together. We have to find the balance between confidence, and to be hungry in training and in games.

"For a long time Tottenham played without this character, now I'm the coach, I want to see this character every week. With the quality, with character, the right energy, I think we're going to win many games and score many goals."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Lionel Messi returns from Argentina farewell as Inter Miami face DC United
articles.summary: Fresh off final game with Argentina, Messi leads Miami against DC United in Major League Soccer in the United States.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi said his farewell to ‌the Argentina national team earlier this week when he played his final match ⁠for the three-time world champions, ending a 21-year international career.

Messi’s ⁠next task will be to break Inter Miami out of their five-match winless streak in Major League Soccer (MLS) when they host DC United on ⁠Saturday.

Inter Miami (12-5-10, 46 points) sit in third place in the Eastern Conference despite being tied in points with New England, as the Revolution hold the tiebreaker with 14 ⁠wins so far.

DC United (6-8-12, 30 points) are in 11th place and need a victory, as they are three points behind the final playoff spot in the conference.

Inter Miami won the Campeones Cup on September 16 in their first match under recently hired coach Kily Gonzalez, but ‌they drew with San Diego and lost 2-1 at Columbus last Sunday in two league matches since.

Messi has been stellar once again this season, with 21 goals and 13 assists in league play as he chases his third consecutive MLS MVP award, but Miami will need more contributors as it has won only once in its last 10 league matches.

“Leo is a person who every day conveys it ⁠and passes it on to his teammates, and he demands from ⁠all of us that you have to be at 100% in every way,” Gonzalez said on Friday.

DC United are also looking to break a three-match winless streak ⁠and win their first match since September 9.

They lost their first match against Miami, 2-1, on March 7 in Baltimore, in a game where Messi and Rodrigo De Paul each scored.

On Tuesday, Messi delivered ‌one last masterclass in the blue and white of Argentina as its most decorated player and captain, by scoring one goal and setting up two others in a 3-0 friendly match against Benin.

The 39-year-old’s final bow came in front of more than 85,000 fans at a packed ⁠Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.

Messi left as the country’s most-capped player (208) and record scorer, having transformed years of frustration on the international stage ‌into ‌a story of World Cup and Copa America triumphs.

articles.title: 'Reminds me of Muller' - Naderi proving worth in Rangers revival
articles.summary: After a slow start to his Rangers career, striker Ryan Naderi is playing an integral role in the club's title challenge and proving his doubters wrong.
articles.body:
A previously unfancied striker is playing a crucial role in Rangers' revival - and even earning comparisons with Germany legend Thomas Muller.

Ryan Naderi pounced for a first-half double against Kilmarnock as Derek McInnes' side overcame the disruption of the extended international break to earn a sixth straight league win and rise to the top of the Scottish Premiership.

That outcome enhanced a turnaround in fortunes for Rangers after the disappointment of their European exit, having also taken just a point from their first two Premiership games.

They now lie a point ahead of Celtic, who visit Motherwell on Sunday under pressure to regain their place at the top.

Much of the focus has centred on an excellent defensive record with just one league goal conceded in their previous five Premiership games - that record blemished by Nicky Clesenco's late Kilmarnock consolation.

However, at the top end of the pitch, Naderi is defying those who doubted his ability to make a consistent impact.

Former Rangers forward Peter Lovenkrands has been impressed by what he's seen from the German-born Czech Republic striker.

"Naderi at times does things where you're like 'How did he do that?'" Lovenkrands said on BBC Sportsound.

"He reminds me a lot of Thomas Muller - he's not nice on the eye at times, but he creates stuff because he's so unorthodox."

Rangers overwhelm Kilmarnock to take top spot

What could Rangers' 2012 case tell us about Man City's uncertain future?

Naderi steps up in absence of Shankland and Chermiti

Naderi now has three goals in his past two league games, having scored the winner in Rangers' 1-0 league win away to Celtic before the break.

That alone elevated his status among an initially sceptical support who had watched the 23-year-old struggle to make an impact after signing from German third-tier side Hansa Rostock in February.

Just one league goal - and two in a League Cup trouncing of Queen's Park - followed last season, with observers unconvinced he had the attributes to be a starting striker at the club.

Such assessments seem to have dissipated as he has surged to the fore in the absence of injured team-mates Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti.

Six goals and three assists, often key interventions, have elevated his status as he adds end product to his physical prowess.

A crucial assist in the late win over St Mirren when Bojan Miovski scored a vital winner was notable.

Naderi has netted winners against Motherwell and Celtic and his two goals against Kilmarnock proved decisive.

His manager agrees Naderi, who made his Czech Republic debut last week, has stepped up to the plate for Rangers at a good time.

"Yes, and fair play to him," McInnes said. "He's always such an honest boy, he's willing to put defenders under pressure.

"I've always felt as a striker that if the ball goes in the box, he'll score his goals. He's not the type of striker that creates a lot for himself, so he needs that service.

"If we put the ball in the box, as we did in the first half, then he looks a threat.

"He's had such a good few weeks. Everybody's so pleased for him. We need someone who would regularly be the goalscorer here at the club."

McInnes cited fatigue and the extended break as reasons for his side not kicking on from leading 3-0 by half-time against Kilmarnock.

The visitors were unfortunate to only pull one goal back as Rangers toiled in the second half.

That said, it's now seven wins in a row in all competitions, with strikers firing backed up by a defensive solidity that might have fans believing this could be their season for a first league title since 2021.

Former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday has more faith now in McInnes' side, telling BBC Sportsound: "A lot of my confidence doesn't come from Rangers being brilliant, it comes from Celtic being poor.

"Rangers are definitely building. They are becoming a much more predictable side - you go into games fancying them to win.

"You're starting to see a Derek McInnes side - really solid defensively and creating chances."

McInnes admitted Rangers' second-half performance was "far from where we needed to be", but wants the club to "feel good about ourselves" after topping the table for the first time this season.

"There's a bit of understanding for me where the players have been. This break's been far too long," he said.

"But we've got the job done, and credit the players for digging deep and getting three points."

articles.title: Gary Neville warns Man Utd players to 'get a grip' or face a worrying few weeks after draw with 10-man Spurs
articles.summary: Man Utd were held to a 1-1 draw by 10-man Spurs, leaving them with one win from six Premier League games; Michael Carrick's side are away to Atletico Madrid and Leeds next; Gary Neville: "If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out"
articles.body:
Michael Carrick's side's poor start to the campaign continued as Dominic Solanke's 92nd-minute goal rescued a point for the 10-man visitors at Old Trafford on Saturday.

There were boos from the home fans, both at half-time and full-time, as United extended their winless run to four games in all competitions, keeping them 12th in the Premier League .

They now face a daunting run of fixtures , starting with a Champions League away game against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday before Sunday's Premier League trip to Elland Road to face Leeds, live on Sky Sports .

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast , Neville questioned the midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo and said the side's plight could worsen if their players do not show improvement.

"Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now," Neville said.

"I'm not calling time on it because that's probably too drastic, but I've seen enough to think that's not a midfield that's dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.

"I think they are both good players individually. But sometimes you just have players that don't quite knit together or don't quite suit each other.

"I think when [Carlos] Baleba came on with Mainoo, it looked like there was a lot more energy.

"There's going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip because they are going to Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid and Elland Road.

"If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out.

"They've got a couple of days to recover, pick themselves up from this and get going, because if they don't get going it's going to be a worrying few weeks."

Neville felt the boos inside Old Trafford were not aimed at head coach Carrick but described the performance as "worrying" and said supporters are picking up on a lack of effort and energy from the players.

"It was worrying because I think the three-week break was the reset moment," he added. "This was the start of a big period of eight games in 28 days.

"What I really would have expected today from Manchester United was a really enthusiastic, energetic performance from minute one.

"I didn't see an enthusiastic, energetic performance from those red shirts for an hour, and Spurs should have been three or four-nil up.

"I think the fans will stay with the project. I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is they're turning quite quickly.

"Manchester United fans are incredibly loyal, beyond loyal, to their managers and to their players, but what they won't accept is a lack of energy.

"They won't accept a lack of what they deem to be effort. I don't like saying effort but the reality is they're not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination, fighting spirit. They're just not.

"They booed after 22 minutes, they booed at half-time and they booed at the end. That tells you that they're really despondent with what they're watching.

"My daughter comes and watches every single week. She texted me at half-time, 'What's that?' My daughter's 16 years of age. You can't kid or con a football fan. No matter who they are, they know what they're watching.

"I don't mind winning here, don't mind losing here, but there's got to be a massive amount of effort and it can't be boring, simple as that.

"You can have a shootout and lose 4-2 and think, 'OK, well at least we saw a Manchester United that went forward with verve and all those things that you'd expect'.

"But what we're seeing at the moment is a team that looks like they're curling up in a ball. For some of them right now, it looks like the club is getting a bit big for them.

"A lot of them played well last season here, but it just looks like now it's coming on top for them a little bit and it's starting to just get to them.

"It did a little bit under Ruben Amorim towards the end where they just started to go a little bit like that.

"So look, Michael Carrick has got to get something out of them, the boos I don't think are against him, but the pressure's on him, the questions are obviously always with the manager and you just hope they can come out of it in these next few weeks."

articles.title: Texas A&M's Mike Elko Rips Local Media Outlet, Addresses Frustrated Fans After Loss to Missouri
articles.summary: Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko called out local media outlet TexAgs while discussing fan frustration following the team's 27-6 loss to No. 14 Missouri on Saturday.
articles.body:
Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko called out local media outlet TexAgs while discussing fan frustration following the team's 27-6 loss to No. 14 Missouri on Saturday.

"There's a difference to me between the fan base and social media," Elko said. "So there's one group that I really don't care much about. Billy's cesspool (at TexAgs) can go be Billy's cesspool. Our fan base, stay with us, be behind us. We're going to build something that we told you we were going to build. So we're in a really bad spot right now, but we'll work our way out of it."

The Aggies suffered their third loss in four games on Saturday. All three defeats featured a double-digit scoring margin. They now sit at 3-3 on the season.

It's understandable that there may be some doubt surrounding Elko's squad.

After the Aggies compiled an 8-5 record during his first season patrolling the sidelines in 2024, they finished at 11-2 and made a College Football Playoff appearance during their 2025 campaign.

Texas A&M was expected to remain among the top teams in the SEC in 2026, as the school was ranked No. 8 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll.

The Aggies struggled in several areas against Missouri on Saturday, allowing the Tigers to total 252 rush yards as a team on 44 attempts.

Texas A&M's offense was only able to muster 216 total yards, converting a mere five of 18 opportunities on third down. Aggies quarterback Marcel Reed finished 19-of-39 for 187 yards while getting picked off twice.

Reed has dealt with inconsistency throughout the beginning of the season. He's now completed 55.3 percent of his throws for 1,095 yards and six touchdowns compared to six interceptions through six starts.

Elko and the Aggies will look to get back on track in their next game, a matchup with The Citadel on Oct. 17.

articles.title: UNC knocks off previously undefeated No. 25 Pitt while notching first ranked win of Bill Belichick era
articles.summary: The Tar Heels erased a 10-0 deficit, and their game-winning touchdown came on a 75-yard catch and run early in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
The second iteration of Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Heels is much more dangerous. UNC hinted at its improvement with a season-opening win over TCU in rainy Dublin back in August .

Although UNC dropped both of those games, program progress was undeniable. The Tar Heels reaped the benefits of that development on Saturday in Pittsburgh, where they defeated the No. 25 Panthers 21-17 , notching the first ranked victory of the Belichick era.

After going 4-8 in Year 1 — a tumultuous campaign that included five multi-score defeats — Belichick is 3-2 this season, with his upgraded UNC squad moving to 1-1 in ACC competition following a triumph in Acrisure Stadium.

"A gutsy performance, you know," said Belichick, 74, in his on-field postgame interview . "Just kept battling. Pitt's a good football team. They're well coached. Some big plays in the game both ways. So luckily we made a couple more than they did."

Later in that interview, Belichick swiftly, and characteristically, turned the page. When asked what's next, he said, "We just get ready for Duke."

The Tar Heels will face the rival Blue Devils next week in Durham.

Granted Pitt (5-1, 2-1 ACC) was playing without the quarterback that was largely responsible for its 5-0 start, as Mason Heintschel was out with the season-ending ACL tear he suffered last week in a victory at Virginia Tech , but a ranked win is a ranked win.

Heintschel's replacement, Holden Geriner, struggled. The fifth-year signal-caller previously spent time at Auburn (2022-24) and Texas State (2025) and came into the weekend with 47 career passes. He nearly matched that workload against UNC yet averaged a mere 5 yards per attempt.

Geriner went 27 of 44 with 219 passing yards and two interceptions. He misfired time and time again when it mattered most in the final frame.

UNC QB Billy Edwards Jr. wasn't perfect, either. That said, he hit tight end Shamar Easter in stride for a go-ahead 75-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter.

From that point on, the Tar Heels' defense hung on to secure the milestone win.

Edwards piled up 249 passing yards, two touchdowns and two picks on 18-of-26 passing. That scoring strike to Easter proved sufficient.

It came on the first snap from scrimmage after a seven-play, 75-yard Pitt touchdown drive that put the Panthers up 17-14 with 12:47 left.

On UNC's next fourth-quarter possession, however, Edwards was intercepted on a pass that was out of reach for wideout Jordan Shipp.

Shadarian Harrison's 22-yard return on that takeaway slingshotted Pitt into Tar Heels territory. What followed was the first of Pitt's three consecutive turnovers on downs.

On fourth-and-2 from the UNC 21-yard line, Geriner's pass was too high for wide receiver Cataurus Hicks to bring down.

The next Panthers series, Pat Narduzzi's team ran tempo leading up to a fourth-and-2 from the Tar Heels' 31. Running back La'Vell Wright was stopped short of the first-down marker, and it initially looked like UNC jarred the ball loose on the play, ostensibly resulting in a 70-yard scoop-and-score that was ultimately overturned.

Pitt got one more crack at orchestrating a game-winning drive. Geriner completed one of his four attempts on that series, and it went for -4 yards.

UNC, which dug itself out of a 10-0 first-half hole, capped the exploit in victory formation.

A Tar Heels program that seemed utterly erratic throughout the first year-plus of the Belichick regime, with general manager Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick both resigning last month, has finally been trending in the right direction lately.

Belichick's UNC is above .500 in October, with a ranked win under its belt.

articles.title: USWNT vs. Spain Score, Highlights, Stats and Reaction
articles.summary: Spain defeated the United States 2-0 on Saturday in a showdown between the two highest-ranked teams in international women's soccer at Audi Field in Washington, D.C.
articles.body:
Spain defeated the United States 2-0 on Saturday in a showdown between the two highest-ranked teams in international women's soccer at Audi Field in Washington, D.C.

No. 1-ranked Spain jumped on the USWNT early, scoring two goals in the first 14 minutes of the match, and leading the rest of the way.

In just the third minute, Spain's Patri Guijarro hit a cracking shot from outside the box to beat goalkeeper Claudia Dickey and put La Roja ahead 1-0:

Just 11 minutes later, Spain struck again when Eva Navarro deposited a perfect cross from Salma Paralluelo:

With that, the Americans found themselves in an unfamiliar position down by two goals.

Steve Goff of Yahoo Sports and Keeper Notes broke down just how uncommon it has been in recent years for the United States to trail by more than one goal, particularly under head coach Emma Hayes:

It momentarily looked as though the U.S. had cut the deficit in half in the 53rd minute, but Sophia Wilson was ruled to be offsides upon VAR review:

The U.S. continued to pour it on in the minutes that followed, and a golden opportunity was earned when Mallory Swanson was hauled down in the box.

However, 19-year-old Lily Yohannes' penalty kick was stonewalled by Spanish goalkeeper Adriana Nanclares, allowing Spain to maintain their 2-0 advantage:

A red card to Spain's Athenea del Castillo in the first minute of stoppage time gave the U.S. some hope, but Spain stood tall and closed out the clean sheet.

While Spain won the possession battle with 54 percent to the United States' 46 percent, the Americans' strong play in the second half resulted in them finishing with 12 shots and nine shots on goal, compared to six and three for Spain.

Saturday's loss continued the trend of uneven play by the USWNT dating back to April.

Over their past six matches, the Americans have won three and lost three with defeats at the hands of Spain, Brazil and Japan.

Meanwhile, Spain's only loss in their past 21 matches came at the hands of England in April.

While Saturday's result was a disappointing one for the Americans, they will have a chance to bounce back quickly when they clash with Spain once again in another friendly Tuesday night in Chester, Pennsylvania.

articles.title: Manchester United: Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on boss Carrick
articles.summary: It couldn't happen again could it? Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on Man Utd boss Michael Carrick after a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur.
articles.body:
For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.

For the third time in as many seasons, a United manager finds himself under severe pressure before the clocks have gone back.

Four weeks ago, Manchester City needed an incorrect video assistant referee (VAR) decision to take advantage of an ineffective United performance after Phil Foden had been shown a red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

On Saturday, the damage was self-inflicted as a Spurs side, who had given every indication of being unable to score before Rodrigo Bentancur's headfirst charge at Luke Shaw just five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's opener, came up with an injury-time equaliser.

Centre-back Lisandro Martinez was outmuscled embarrassingly easily by Dominic Solanke, with goalkeeper Senne Lammens failing to read the striker's deft touch that crept in at the far corner.

The anguish on United faces told its own story.

"A worrying day for Michael Carrick," observed former United skipper Gary Neville on Sky Sports.

Late Solanke strike salvages 10-man Spurs draw at Man Utd

Tottenham grab a draw but who got 1/10 - Ratings for Man Utd v Spurs

Manchester United have just six points from their opening six games of the Premier League season, their fewest at this stage of a league campaign since 1986-87, when they amassed four under Sir Alex Ferguson.

They have failed to win five of their six Premier League games this season (D3 L2), already as many as in 17 league games under Michael Carrick last season (W12 D3 L2).

United have collected two points from their last two games, both of which were against teams who began the match at the bottom of the Premier League.

In points terms they are closer to the relegation zone than the Champions League spots.

Carrick's side are now winless in four league games and face an always tricky trip across the Pennines to face old rivals Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday, 18 October. Either side of that are daunting Champions League trips to Atletico Madrid and Como.

United officials have repeatedly offered their backing to Carrick in recent weeks.

However, no fan needs reminding that two seasons ago a run of two wins in nine games in all competitions put Erik ten Hag under severe pressure before the axe fell after a defeat at West Ham on 27 October.

Last season, a combination of a shocking EFL Cup exit at the hands of League Two Grimsby and an insipid 3-1 loss at Brentford on 27 September did so much to undermine confidence in Ruben Amorim before he was sacked on 5 January.

The start to this campaign is starting to look increasingly familiar.

"I'm not happy with he amount of points we've got so far, for sure, you know," said Carrick.

"I'm not hiding, there's no hiding from that. I think it could have been different for a couple of little things here or there, but the reality is the reality, we've got to accept it, you know. We need to put things in a direction, in a positive direction quite quickly, that's pretty plain."

The 'little things' Carrick talks about are the defending for Solanke's goal, the lack of pressure put on Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles when he smashed another injury-time equaliser at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on 6 September, and the preventable Martinez own goal that nearly gave Fulham victory at Craven Cottage just before the international break.

"We've got to be a little bit more streetwise in moments, a little bit more stubborn and a little bit stronger in seeing out certain things," he added.

"It doesn't change my belief or the confidence in the players, you know. We're a really good team and capable of being a really good team, but we've obviously got to start getting more points on the board, that's for sure."

The problem is with each disappointment, the belief of United being 'a really good team' starts to ebb away.

Yet again, a post-match focus centred on how much Carrick's team ran, even though running for the sake of it has proved to be of little benefit.

"The stats don't lie when every time the other team runs more than you," said Sky Sports pundit and former Spurs captain Jamie Redknapp.

"Tottenham ran 5km more than Man United. OK, they had 10 men but that is every game. If you outrun your opposing number, you will win games. I'm not saying they are not trying. It is that physical battle they are losing though."

While, ex-Spurs midfielder Danny Murphy, added on BBC Match of the Day: "There was a lethargy about Man Utd, this midfield can't control games. It is partly tactical and partly personnel.

"I don't understand it. We saw at the end of last season Man Utd were much more organised and much more difficult to play against.

"The space in midfield was incredible and if they were playing against a more competent side, they would have been beaten. Play like that against good teams and they will be cut wide open."

It feels as though some fans are losing faith already, judging by the way they reacted at moments during the game, aside from the boos that accompanied the end of each half.

Forward Matheus Cunha - one of a number of Carrick's squad who have failed to reproduce the form he showed in the second half of last season - gestured to the crowd during the opening period. It wasn't clear whether he was responding to a negative comment or urging more noise, but the Brazilian clearly wasn't happy.

Carrick's family are season ticket holders. He knows what it is like to watch United struggle at Old Trafford.

"Obviously, it hurts," he said. "It hurts a lot. It's not nice to go through. I care as much as anybody about this place. Sometimes you could say too much because then it overspills. But it's coming from a good place, really, and so I understand it."

It is in moments like this that Carrick, who presents such a calm front in public, must be churning inside.

He knows how the pressure can mount around Old Trafford and how fierce the debate around the club in the search for answers can be.

As he said, Carrick cares. And he is certain his players feel the same.

"I don't feel let down," he added. "You can make mistakes.

"We've all got standards; we've all got levels. The players hold their hands up at times when something goes against them.

"It's not like everyone walks off into the distance tonight like everything's fine and it's left on me. It's not that at all. The players care, for sure.

"I don't feel let down by them for making a mistake. We've just got to all help each other be better, and it's on me to help them and guide them through it."

Pre-match, post-match and topical United content

articles.title: 'I kissed Rodrigo' - Roberto de Zerbi praises Bentancur's red card against Manchester United
articles.summary: Roberto de Zerbi praises Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.
articles.body:
Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi praised Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United .

The Uruguay midfielder was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a feisty 78th-minute melee when Spurs were trailing 1-0 at Old Trafford.

Despite being reduced to 10 men, Tottenham managed to salvage a point as Dominic Solanke headed home in the second minute of added time.

Spurs remain winless in the Premier League this season after six games, but De Zerbi was thankful to Bentancur for providing a "spark" against United.

"I kiss Rodrigo and say thanks," De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference.

"In that moment maybe with 10 players we played with more courage, more energy.

"For a long time Tottenham played without this blood, this character."

The incident happened when Shaw, on the receiving end of a reckless challenge by Bentancur, raced towards the Spurs player and shoved him off the pitch.

Bentancur reacted by planting his head towards Shaw's face. The pair were separated by their team-mates before referee Stuart Attwell sent the substitute off.

De Zerbi said it was a "mistake" by Bentancur, but added it was the type of reaction Tottenham needed to finish the game.

"I kissed Bentancur in the dressing room because we need this type of reaction, this character. Football is character," he told Sky Sports.

"I liked the situation with the red card. We need at this moment the situation, not to bring a red card but we need to not accept the defeat."

'First time we played like a team' - could this be a turning point for Spurs?

Despite the late elation sparked by Solanke's 92nd-minute equaliser, Tottenham remain in the relegation zone with just three points from their opening six matches.

It is just the fourth time the club have failed to win each of their opening six games of a league season, after 2008-09, 1955-56 and 1912-13.

Spurs have often looked lively in attack this season, but they have lacked conviction in front of goal and only 19th-placed Coventry have scored fewer goals than Tottenham 's three.

However, Tottenham fans can take belief from their overall performance at Old Trafford as they ran United ragged in the opening half with fluid, high-tempo football.

"Today has been the game where for the first time this season we showed we are a team," De Zerbi said.

"We played for the team-mates, we played together, we stayed inside of the game in every situation and we attacked as a team and defended as a team."

The Italian manager added on Sky Sports: "I'm very happy because I've seen the right spirit, the right character and I want to start from this character, this reaction, this behaviour."

Tottenham spent more than £250m on new talent over the summer - adding 10 players to their squad.

But their poor start has prompted the club to organise a warm-weather training camp in Spain, with the team expected to travel to Marbella on Sunday in the hope it will provide a chance for their new-look squad to bond.

"Now the target is to build the team," De Zerbi said.

"We are a great group of players but we are not a team yet and to be a team is to play for the team-mates, suffer together, attack together."

Spurs face newly-promoted Coventry on Monday, 19 October before making the short trip to Chelsea the following Saturday.

articles.title: Iñigo: “Nos ha faltado rematar un partido redondo”
articles.standfirst: El técnico amarillo se fue contento con el juego de su equipo pese a la derrota
articles.summary: El técnico amarillo se fue contento con el juego de su equipo pese a la derrota
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez lamentó que su equipo no tuviese más pegada en ataque para poner la guinda a lo que considera un buen partido de su equipo. El navarro destacó el partido de sus mediocentros, en especial de Juan Foyth Faltó rematar el trabajo: “Creo que en ese momento final siempre nos pasa a todo el mundo cuando ves que estás haciendo cosas bien, ves que el gol está cerca, pero que también el tiempo se termina, se genera un mayor crispación de la que hay hay en el ambiente, que es normal, por como ha sido el partido y lo que es el fútbol, el poder hacer las cosas bien, se diluye y pasa a un segundo plano. Es difícil. Debo escuchar a los jugadores porque en ese sentido es difícil estar ahí abajo uno también siente que por momentos pierde el control con el cuarto y es complejo, pero sí, estoy de acuerdo que nos ha faltado rematar, nunca mejor dicho y tener acierto para hacer un partido redondísimo” Foyth de mediocentro: “Con la inclusión de Juan de 6, es una evidencia que buscas solidificar un poco el centro del campo, sabiendo que en este escenario si tú no dominas el centro del campo, tanto en ataque como en defensa, ellos empiezan a correr y empiezan a sentirse libres, cómodos y es donde el entrenador poco puede hacer en el tema de defender una transición del Real Madrid. Después con balón también nos da muchísimas conexiones, opciones de pase, los tres que han jugado por dentro tienen capacidad física y técnica para hacerlo. Creo que hemos estado cómodos pero creo que por momentos podríamos haber hecho todavía más daño con la posesión, con desesperarles. Es cierto que he visto un Real Madrid implicado, ha sido costoso salir de su presión y en ese sentido creo que estoy contento con cómo han jugado los tres medios centros. El planteamiento del Madrid: “Cuando venimos de tantas semanas de inactividad antes de ver la alineación, siempre esperas que pueda ocurrir este tipo de cambios, porque durante unas semanas los vas pensando tú mismo, jugadores que se van incorporando por goteo, sabiendo que unos han jugado mucho, otros poco y los viajes son muy largos. Todo este tipo de circunstancias pues sabe que el rival también está en ello y este escenario que ha sucedido lo podíamos prever. Los parones del final: “Comentaba en la primera pregunta que la crispación de la alta tensión en un partido como el que hemos vivido con dos equipos que quieren imponerse al otro sin ningún reparo, con las cartas descubiertas, Es normal, el resultado corto, el tiempo apremia, defiendes tu resultado en tu casa, nosotros queremos ganar. No me sorprende lo que ha sucedido, es fruto del fútbol y creo que hay que darle cierta naturalidad más allá de que hay gente que se encarga de ordenar este tipo de tensión” Ganaron todas las estadísticas: “Entiendo lo que me dices y cuando pasen unas horas seguramente ese tipo de parámetros los miraremos y refrendarán el gran partido que ha hecho los jugadores, pero con el ardor de la batalla nunca mejor dicho, todavía latente aquí me cuesta sacar esa parte positiva. Pero soy consciente del gran partido que hemos hecho como equipo ante un rival tan complejo y en un escenario en el que siempre ve uno cuando está desde fuera las dificultades que el equipo rival tiene. Las transiciones del Madrid: “Creo que las transiciones del Real Madrid esta temporada con su entrenador, que ha sido un especialista también en la época que estuvo aquí, lo he sufrido de jugador, son difíciles de frenar. Es como siempre han transitado y como cada vez que tú pierdes el balón aquí te penalizan. Entonces, ese es el punto número uno sabiendo que cuando enfrentas al Real Madrid y el Bernabéu no puedes centrarse solo en un aspecto a controlar. Hay muchos individuales colectivos de ambiente. Ese es uno, pero bueno, ha ha habido diferentes, pero creo que ese es el que todos cuando sentamos en la televisión podemos ver que es un punto fuerte de ellos” Punto de frustración: “Sí, es frustrante. Los jugadores han adquirido esta idea de poder venir a estos escenarios, evitar un poco el temor que aparece, pero ya ven que puedes hacerlo y que estás cerca de ganar. Entonces, cuando no lo consigues, habiendo merecido, por lo menos algo más, pues es frustrante, pero bueno, debemos seguir en esta línea, sobre todo mental y emocional de poder plantear un partido así que ellos crean en la idea y que luego ojalá poder ayudarles para que en la táctica estén cómodos.” Proceso: “Este club lleva décadas al más alto nivel. Yo soy el que debe adaptarse más allá de que tenga una idea propia. Si tengo que venir a jugar a un escenario como este, el reflejo que me queda es muy positivo. He visto a los jugadores coincidiendo con lo que un entrenador les ha dicho, con lo que está sucediendo, sobre todo a nivel de idea de juego, a nivel de donde nos movemos, cómo nos paramos cómo no entonces es la no es el día perfecto para ver de esto, pero sí, entiendo que es algo que no solo se tiene que hablar de Iñigo, sino que va más allá de él.

articles.title: El acta de Díaz de Mera detalla la expulsión de Vinicius: "Actitud agresiva" y protestas "a voz en grito"
articles.standfirst: El colegiado describió la "actitud agresiva" del brasileño al protestar su expulsión por el tirón de pelo, un relato que apunta a una sanción que podría dejarle sin el duelo ante el Barça
articles.summary: El colegiado describió la "actitud agresiva" del brasileño al protestar su expulsión por el tirón de pelo, un relato que apunta a una sanción que podría dejarle sin el duelo ante el Barça
articles.body: El acta arbitral del partido entre el Real Madrid y el Villarreal (1-0), disputado este sábado en el Santiago Bernabéu, recogió con detalle la expulsión de Vinicius Júnior y las protestas posteriores del delantero brasileño. El colegiado del encuentro, Díaz de Mera, reflejó en el documento tanto el motivo de la roja como un episodio adicional ya con el jugador expulsado. Sobre la tarjeta, el acta explicó que Vinicius fue expulsado en el minuto 73 “por tirar del pelo a un adversario, con el balón en juego, sin estar el balón en disputa entre ellos”. La acción se produjo en la jugada en la que el brasileño había enviado el balón a la red, en un tanto que el colegiado anuló al apreciar esa infracción previa. El árbitro añadió un apartado de “otras incidencias” en el que relató lo sucedido tras la expulsión. “En el minuto 73 de partido, estando el juego detenido, el jugador del club local número 7 D. Vinicius José De Oliveira Do Nascimento, después de haber sido expulsado y encontrándose aún en el terreno de juego, siguió protestando mi decisión, a voz en grito, dirigiéndose a la zona donde me encontraba con actitud agresiva”, escribió Díaz de Mera. El colegiado precisó, además, que el delantero “tuvo que ser sujetado por compañeros de su equipo”, aunque matizó que no pudo “apreciar ninguna expresión concreta”. El relato del acta, sumado al protocolo del CTA, invita a pensar que la sanción podría ir más allá de un solo partido y, por ende, Vinicius se perdería el Clásico ante el Barcelona del próximo 25 de octubre. El Madrid solo disputa un encuentro liguero entre medias, ante el Sevilla, por lo que un castigo de dos o más partidos dejaría al brasileño fuera de la cita en el Camp Nou. El acta no se limitó a Vinicius. El árbitro también mostró amonestación a José Mourinho y al delegado Chendo, y expulsó al entrenador de porteros del Real Madrid, Nuno Santos, en una noche de máxima tensión en el banquillo blanco con las decisiones arbitrales. Por parte del Villarreal, el colegiado expulsó a Xisco Nadal, delegado Villarreal. El protocolo del CTA incluye el tirón de pelo dentro de la categoría CV.1, la de conducta violenta, que agrupa las acciones en las que un “jugador propina un codazo, cabezazo, puñetazo, bofetón, agarra del cuello, empujón, patada, coz, mordisco, tirón de pelo… a un contrario o cualquier otra persona sin estar disputando el balón, empleando fuerza excesiva o brutalidad”. Este tipo de acciones por conducta violenta suelen acarrear una sanción de más de un partido, un castigo que dejaría al brasileño sin el Clásico ante el Barcelona, ya que entre medias el Madrid solo disputa el duelo liguero frente al Sevilla.

articles.title: Los ferrolanos asaltaron Riazor gracias a su mayor oficio
articles.standfirst: Un tanto de Ropero al filo del descanso decantó el encuentro a favor de los verdes
articles.summary: Un tanto de Ropero al filo del descanso decantó el encuentro a favor de los verdes
articles.body: El fútbol rara vez atiende a razones. En la séptima jornada del Grupo 1 de Primera Federación, el Deportivo Fabril firmó un partido de dominio aplastante —70% de posesión, 24 remates, 11 córneres— y acabó con las manos vacías. El Racing de Ferrol, replegado, superado en casi todas las estadísticas y reducido a diez durante la última media hora, se llevó los tres puntos gracias a un solitario tanto de Unai Ropero justo antes del descanso. Un 0-1 que resume a la perfección por qué el fútbol es un deporte de áreas y no de datos. FICHA TÉCNICA Fabril: Hugo Ríos; Álvaro Mardones (Pablo García, 71‘), Samu Fernández, Quique Teijo, Íker Vidal; Koke San José (Dani Estévez, 78’), Rubén López, Álvaro Fraga (Mejía, 71’); Adrián Guerrero (Leandro Altieri, 78’), Justino Barbosa (David Domínguez, 61’) e Íker Gil. Racing de Ferrol: Lucas Díaz; Migue Leal, Eric Monjonell, Ger Nóvoa, Álvaro Ramón; Fabio González, Vicente Esquerdo (Jesús Bernal, 54’); Raúl Blanco (Saúl García, 73’), Unai Ropero (Roberto Arroyo, 54’), Dani Ojeda (David Castro, 73’) y Ettiene Eto’o (Raúl Alcaina, 62’). Goles: 0-1 Unai Ropero (44′). Árbitro: Ekaitz Ikiñi García (colegio vasco). Amonestó a Quique Teijo y Samu Fernández del Deportivo Fabril y a Raúl Blanco, Fabio Gonzálezy Dani Ojeda del Racing de Ferrol. Además, expulsó por doble amarilla a Álvaro Ramón del Racing de Ferrol a los 66 minutos. Incidencias: Estadio Riazor (A Coruña). Partido correspondiente a la séptima jornada de Primera Federación. Un primer acto que torció el guion local El filial deportivista salió a mandar y lo consiguió desde el pitido inicial. El balón vivió en los pies del equipo coruñés, que acumuló pases (601 por los 257 del rival, con 540 completados) y empujó una y otra vez hacia el área visitante. Pero el Racing golpeó cuando menos se lo esperaba nadie: en el minuto 44, con el descanso a la vuelta de la esquina, Unai Ropero definió para poner el 0-1 que resultaría definitivo. Fue una de las dos ocasiones claras que generaron los ferrolanos en todo el encuentro —las dos únicas que registraron— frente a un Fabril que, pese a la montaña de llegadas, no fue capaz de materializar ni una sola ocasión manifiesta. Ropero fue sustituido en el 54 por Roberto Arroyo, pero su obra ya estaba hecha: tres disparos, dos de ellos a puerta, y el único que contó. Un Fabril que chocó una y otra vez contra Lucas Díaz Si hay un nombre que explica por qué el dominio local no se tradujo en goles, es el del guardameta visitante Lucas Díaz. El meta del Racing firmó una actuación sobresaliente —valorada con un 8,4, la más alta del partido— con seis paradas, dos de ellas a remates desde dentro del área. Fue el muro contra el que se estrelló toda la producción ofensiva coruñesa. Porque el Fabril generó, y mucho. De sus 24 disparos, seis fueron entre los tres palos, aunque hasta catorce se marcharon fuera, síntoma de una pegada imprecisa en los metros decisivos. En el 90, además, el VAR revisó una posible pena máxima a favor de los locales que finalmente no se señaló, cerrando de forma cruel una tarde de impotencia en Abegondo. Entre los locales brilló el central Enrique Teijo, el mejor valorado de los suyos (8,5), con 102 pases acertados de 108, cuatro remates y una presencia defensiva constante. También destacó Samu Fernandez (rating de 8), dueño de 109 toques y de 80 pases buenos desde la zaga. El esfuerzo colectivo fue evidente; la eficacia, inexistente. La expulsión que no cambió el marcador Cuando el Racing se quedó con diez, parecía que el asedio acabaría por abrir el muro. En el minuto 66, Álvaro Ramón vio la segunda amarilla, ratificada por el VAR al minuto siguiente, y dejó a los visitantes en inferioridad numérica para los últimos 24 minutos reglamentarios más el añadido. El lateral se marchó con un flojo 5,7 de valoración, lastrado por sus tres faltas y por el error que derivó en un remate rival. La indisciplina marcó el pulso visitante: cinco tarjetas amarillas y una roja para el Racing, por solo dos amonestaciones del Fabril. Pero ni con uno más sobre el césped encontró el conjunto local la grieta. El Racing se parapetó —32 despejes, con Germán Novoa (10) y Eric Monjonell (7) multiplicándose atrás— y aguantó el chaparrón hasta el final. Lo que dice la clasificación El resultado tiene lecturas opuestas para ambos. El Racing de Ferrol, con siete jornadas disputadas, suma 13 puntos (4 victorias, 1 empate, 2 derrotas) y se afianza en la tercera plaza del Grupo 1, a tres de los dos colíderes, UD Logroñés y CD Lugo, ambos con 16 puntos pero habiendo jugado un partido menos. La cima sigue al alcance. El Deportivo Fabril, en cambio, se queda en 8 puntos (2 victorias, 2 empates, 3 derrotas) y ocupa la undécima posición, en una zona media-baja donde la igualdad es máxima: hasta seis equipos comparten esos ocho puntos o menos muy cerca del descenso. Para un filial que compite como el que más pero paga caro su falta de puntería, la diferencia de goles de 0 (8 a favor, 8 en contra) retrata su temporada: competitivo, pero sin premio. El dato que duele El Fabril se marcha de su propio estadio tras un partido en el que ganó la posesión (70%-30%), los remates (24-7), los córneres (11-2) y las entradas al último tercio (81-49), y en el que incluso jugó con un futbolista más durante media hora. Y aun así perdió. El fútbol, a veces, premia la contundencia por encima del trabajo: al Racing le bastaron dos ocasiones para fabricar una, la de Ropero, y defenderla con uñas, dientes y un portero en estado de gracia. Al Fabril, veinticuatro disparos no le dieron ni para empatar. Una lección dura para los coruñeses, que tendrán que convertir el dominio en goles si quieren salir cuanto antes del atasco clasificatorio. Para el Racing, en cambio, el mensaje es otro: en Primera Federación, a veces, ganar feo también cuenta como ganar.

articles.title: Nizar se convierte en el noveno vila-realense en jugar en Primera
articles.standfirst: El futbolista de 21 años destaca esta temporada en el filial de David Albelda
articles.summary: El futbolista de 21 años destaca esta temporada en el filial de David Albelda
articles.body: Nízar El Jmili Ben Hamou (Vila-real, 30/11/2004) vivió una noche inolvidable pese la derrota de su equipo. Y es que el canterano se convirtió en el último futbolista de la cantera amarilla en debutar con el Villarreal. Un privilegio por hacerlo en un escenario como el Santiago Bernabéu y por conseguirlo en el equipo de su localidad: Vila-real. Pese a tratarse de una localidad pequeña en comparación con las capitales que suelen actuar en Primera, Vila-real (con poco más de 50 mil habitantes), puede presumir de haber tenido ya a nueve jugadores nacidos allí que han debutado en la máxima categoría del fútbol nacional. Aunque no todos ellos lo hicieron con la camiseta amarilla. Para remontarse al primer caso hay que hacerlo hasta el primer tercio del siglo pasado, cuando el guardameta Ramón Nebot vivió su estreno con la camiseta del Real Madrid. Fue un 1 de diciembre de 1929 cuando participó de la derrota blanca en San Mamés por dos tantos a uno. Posteriormente, en la temporada 62/63, el defensa Vicente Nebot debutó con el CD Condal ante el Mallorca. Ya en la década de los 80 Alfredo Monfort lo conseguía de la mano del CD Castellón. Tras una gran carrera en el club albinegro, Monfort acabó su trayectoria en el Villarreal, pero fue jugando en Segunda. En la misma época y también con el Castellón actuó Juan José Verdú. En la era reciente se ha producido la explosión de la cantera amarilla, y con ella la llegada de varios jugadores nacidos en la localidad. De la mano de Benito Floro, y ya con el Villarreal, debutaron en la temporada 2002/03 tanto César Árzo como Héctor Font, dos de los estandartes de la prolífica ciudad deportiva castellonense. Un testigo que recogería Pau Torres en 2017, seguramente el mejor exponente de todos ellos merced a sus logros. El último jugador nacido en Vila-real que tuvo minutos fue Carlo Adriano durante un Villarreal 5- Levante 0 de la temporada 21/22. Un honor que ahora corresponde a Nizar, quien ha aprovechado el trabajo durante el parón con el primer equipo para convencer al técnico navarro

articles.title: Un gran Zarco frenó al Alcorcón
articles.standfirst: Un gol de cabeza de Joserra al filo del descanso dio los tres puntos al equipo aragonés
articles.summary: Un gol de cabeza de Joserra al filo del descanso dio los tres puntos al equipo aragonés
articles.body: Hay partidos que se ganan con el balón y otros que se ganan sin él. El CD Teruel eligió el segundo camino y lo recorrió hasta el final para asestar un golpe de autoridad a uno de los grandes del Grupo 2. Con apenas un 36% de posesión, seis remates en todo el encuentro y un portero convertido en figura, los turolenses derribaron a un AD Alcorcón que mandó en el juego pero se estrelló una y otra vez contra la realidad del marcador. El único tanto, obra de Joserra de Diego antes del descanso, bastó para dar a los locales tres puntos de oxígeno puro. FICHA TÉCNICA CD TERUEL: Zarco, Andrés Borge, Nathan, Álvaro López, Joserra, Redón (Borikó, min. 61), Albisua, Relu, Sesé (Pablo Felipe, min. 93), Edu Gallardo (Goyo, min. 86) y Sergio Moreno (Romera, min. 86). AD ALCORCÓN: Bañuz, Irurita, Gaixas (Pol, min. 78), Lancho, Rivera (Melero, min. 45), Cuesta, Vacas, Berlanga (Ibáñez, min. 78), Aparicio, Davo (Sabina, min. 78) y Omar. GOL: 1-0, min. 42, Joserra. ÁRBITRO: Oltra Sáez (catalán). Amonestó a Redón, Edu Gallardo, Borge, Albisua Relu por parte del CD Teruel y a Rivera, Aparicio, Cuesta, Davo, Lancho y Melero, de la AD Alcorcón. INCIDENCIAS: Partido disputado en campo Pinilla. Un gol contra corriente justo antes del descanso El Alcorcón salió a imponer su jerarquía y lo consiguió en todo salvo en lo esencial. Los alfareros acumularon amonestaciones tempranas —Pablo Rivera al minuto 24, Esteban Aparicio en el 31, en una acción revisada por el VAR que elevó la tarjeta— mientras buscaban abrir la lata. Pero fue el Teruel quien golpeó cuando menos se esperaba. En el minuto 42, Edu Gallardo inventó la asistencia que valió el partido y Joserra de Diego, central de profesión, apareció para firmar el 1-0 con el que se llegó al descanso. Fue, literalmente, la única gran ocasión que generó el Teruel en todo el encuentro, y la transformó. A partir de ahí, el guion quedó escrito: un Alcorcón volcado y un Teruel replegado, dispuesto a defender su tesoro con uñas y dientes. El dominio estéril de un Alcorcón sin puntería Las estadísticas dibujan un partido de un solo equipo… en todo menos en el resultado. El Alcorcón firmó un 64% de posesión, 24 remates por solo 6 de su rival, nueve tiros a puerta y nueve córners frente a tres. La diferencia en el circuito de pase fue abismal: 475 pases de los visitantes por 271 de los locales. El problema para los de la visita se resume en un dato demoledor: cuatro ocasiones claras falladas y ninguna materializada. El mediapunta Luis Vacas fue el gran director de la ofensiva alcorconera, con una nota sobresaliente de 8,3, cinco pases clave y seis faltas recibidas. A su lado, Omar Ouhdadi repartió cuatro ocasiones de gol y el capitán Esteban Aparicio otras seis desde la banda, pero la pólvora estuvo mojada. Arnau Gaixas, defensa lanzado al ataque, desperdició dos ocasiones claras él solo. La pizarra se llenó de llegadas y se vació de goles. Amador Zarco, el nombre del partido Si el Teruel se llevó los tres puntos fue, en gran medida, por su portero. Amador Zarco completó una actuación de otra dimensión: seis paradas, cinco de ellas a disparos desde dentro del área, una nota de 9 —la más alta del encuentro— y la sensación de que el 1-0 era una fortaleza inexpugnable mientras él siguiera bajo palos. En el otro arco, Miguel Bañuz apenas tuvo que intervenir una vez: resumen perfecto de lo desigual que fue el reparto de trabajo. El héroe defensivo tuvo escudero en el capitán Relu, que firmó un partidazo de resistencia (nota de 8,6) con tres despejes sobre la línea, seis bloqueos y una entrega total en cada balón dividido. Entre el muro humano y las manos de Amador, el Alcorcón se topó con una pared que no cedió ni en los minutos finales, cuando el tramo decisivo se convirtió en una sucesión de tarjetas: hasta cinco amarillas vieron los locales y seis los visitantes en un duelo áspero y trabado. Lo que cambia en la clasificación El resultado tiene lecturas muy distintas para cada vestuario. El AD Alcorcón desaprovecha la oportunidad de pelear por lo más alto: con 12 puntos (3 victorias, 3 empates y 1 derrota) se queda tercero en el Grupo 2, a tres de un líder, el Real Zaragoza, que suma 15. Pese al traspié, los alfareros mantienen la mejor diferencia de goles de todo el grupo (+8), síntoma de que su problema del sábado fue puntual: puntería, no estructura. Para el CD Teruel, la victoria es casi un balón de oxígeno. Los turolenses, instalados en la zona baja con 5 puntos (1 victoria, 2 empates, 4 derrotas) y antepenúltimos en el puesto 17, suman apenas su primer triunfo del curso y empiezan a mirar hacia arriba desde el pozo. Con solo 3 goles a favor y 12 en contra antes de esta jornada, el equipo sabe que su camino pasa precisamente por noches como esta: defender con orden y aprovechar la ocasión que caiga. Lo que dejó el partido La gran paradoja de la tarde es que los dos jugadores más determinantes defendieron camisetas opuestas en el reparto de méritos: Vacas, intratable con el balón pero sin premio, y Amador Zarco, el portero que convirtió el dominio rival en frustración. Joserra de Diego, con su gol y una nota de 7,8, se llevó la gloria discreta del central que decide un partido en el área contraria. El Teruel demostró que, en una categoría tan igualada, un plan claro y un portero inspirado pueden más que la estadística. El Alcorcón, por su parte, se marcha de Aragón con la lección de que dominar no es ganar. Tendrá que afinar la mira si quiere seguir en la conversación por el ascenso; el margen, con el Zaragoza y el Villarreal B escapándose, empieza a estrecharse.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Man City: the top five clashes between Premier League giants
articles.summary: Liverpool face Manchester City on Sunday in what has become a battle between the EPL’s dominant teams in recent times.
articles.body:
The rivalry between Manchester City and Liverpool will be renewed when they meet in Sunday’s supercharged Premier League clash at Anfield.

History suggests Liverpool are often favourites in this fixture, but recent form heavily favours the Manchester club.

City, who have dominated headlines in recent weeks over serious financial breach charges , lead the league’s points table with 15 points – six ahead of Liverpool, who are sixth in the standings.

Sunday’s match will be the 202nd fixture between the teams across all competitions, with Liverpool firmly leading the head-to-head with 95 victories, while City have won 53 matches with 53 drawn.

As Enzo Maresca faces off with Andoni Iraola this weekend, Al Jazeera looks back at the top five clashes over the years:

Liverpool 4-3 Manchester City (January 14, 2018 – Premier League)

Our list begins with this seven-goal league thriller from eight years ago.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain gave Liverpool an early lead that night at Anfield before Roberto Firmino, Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah scored in a rousing eight-minute spell in the second half to build a staggering 4-1 lead.

But Man City struck twice in the final six minutes through Bernardo Silva and Ilkay Gundogan, forcing Liverpool to hold on for a nervous finish.

That result not only strengthened Liverpool’s top-four bid but also ended City’s unbeaten run that season.

Nonetheless, City went on to lift the title that term with a record-breaking 100 points, while Liverpool came fourth.

Liverpool 3-2 Manchester City (April 13, 2014 – Premier League)

This game goes further back in history and it’s another laden with goals.

On the 25th anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster when 97 Liverpool supporters died, a 10-man Liverpool side beat City 3-2 in a dramatic title-race clash.

Early goals by Raheem Sterling and Martin Skrtel put Liverpool in control, but City fought back through David Silva and a Glen Johnson own goal before Philippe Coutinho struck the winner for Liverpool 12 minutes from time.

Coutinho pounced on a loose clearance by City’s Vincent Kompany in the box, drilling the ball into the bottom corner as Anfield went wild for the ‘Little Magician’.

The victory marked a huge step towards Liverpool’s title charge, but ultimately it was City who won the league that season, finishing two points ahead of the Merseyside club.

Manchester City 2-1 Liverpool (January 3, 2019 – Premier League)

The next game on our list sees City on the winning side.

Sergio Aguero had given City the lead with his first-half strike before Firmino equalised four minutes from the hour -mark.

But Leroy Sane won the three vital points for the hosts, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute.

After a quick counterattack, Sterling picked out the onrushing Sane on the left side, just outside the box, before the German’s left-footed shot hit the inside of the post and the ball rolled into the bottom corner.

With that, Liverpool suffered their first loss of the season, ending a 20-game unbeaten streak.

City also went on to reduce Liverpool’s lead at the top to four points and eventually lifted the trophy, beating the Reds by just one point.

Liverpool 3-1 Manchester City (November 10, 2019 – Premier League)

This match goes back to the season that was the first to be affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Goals from Fabinho, Salah and Mane guided the Reds to a hugely impressive 3-1 home win over the title holders.

The match is best remembered by Liverpool fans for Fabinho’s stunning goal, as the Brazilian launched the ball into the net from about 25 yards (23 metres) out.

The result also opened up an eight-point lead at the top of the table and went down as a defining moment in Liverpool’s campaign as they ended their 30-year quest to win the league.

That season, Liverpool finished with 99 points, a whopping 18 points ahead of second-placed City.

Liverpool 3-0 Manchester City (April 4, 2018 – Champions League quarterfinal, first leg)

Our top five list ends with a Champions League clash.

Liverpool fired three goals in the opening half-hour, ripping through their opponents in the first leg of this UCL quarterfinal clash.

Once again, Salah, Mane and Oxlade-Chamberlain were among the scorers as Liverpool took control of the knockout tie.

Oxlade-Chamberlain’s fierce finish – a thundering strike from outside the box – was the highlight of this fixture.

Liverpool went on to reach the final, where they fell to Real Madrid.
